verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.59, VSAQ 142). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Taking a drug in excess, or taking it for a
purpose other than its medicinal use, is called
steps.why: The definition has two separate arms, too much of a medicine and the wrong purpose for a medicine, and a student who writes only one of them has written half the definition.
common_mistakes: Writing that any use of a drug is drug abuse. Medicinal use in the correct dose is not abuse.
Confusing it with addiction. Abuse is the act of taking; addiction is the attachment to the effect.
steps.memory_tip: Two arms: wrong amount, or right amount for the wrong reason.
steps.margin_note: One sentence carrying both arms. Do not stop after 'in excess'.

steps.label: Result
lines: Drug abuse leads to physical and psychological
Sometimes it causes damage to the body that
steps.why: The second mark is for what abuse does, and naming both the body and the mind keeps the answer from repeating the definition in other words.
common_mistakes: Repeating the definition instead of stating the result.
Writing only 'it is bad for health'. Name the physical and the psychological damage.
steps.memory_tip: Damage on two sides: the body and the mind.
steps.margin_note: Two short lines. Name both kinds of damage.

insider_note: A two-mark definition question expects a definition AND its consequence; a one-line definition alone caps the answer at one mark.
